 GURBIR SINGH, J. :
1. CM-20886-C-II of 2023 : This is application under Section 151 CPC for condonation of delay of 14 days in re-filing the present appeal.
For the reasons mentioned in the application, the same is allowed and delay of 14 days in re-filing the present appeal is condoned.
The application stands disposed of.
2. CM-20887-C-II of 2023 and Main Appeal :

The National Insurance Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as - the Insurance Company) has preferred the present appeal against Award dated 21.07.2023, passed by learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Palwal (for brevity - the Tribunal), wherein the appellant Insurance Company has been directed to make payment of compensation to the tune of Rs.22,55,900/- to the claimants on account of death of Ashok Kumar in a motor vehicular 2024:PHHC:023440 accident.

3. The brief facts, necessary for decision of this appeal, are that on 21.01.2020, Ashok Kumar (since deceased) and his cousin brother namely Bharat Pal were going to their village Sujwari from Palwal on motorcycle bearing registration No.HR-30-R-5910.

At about 07:00 PM, near village Ganniki,
Ashok Kumar parked his motorcycle on right side at kachha portion of the right side for urination purpose.

In the meantime, another motorcycle bearing registration No.HR-52-F-3301 (in short - the National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Suman And Others on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130850349/
1 offending vehicle), being driven at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner, came from Palwal side and hit Ashok Kumar, who fell down and sustained multiple injuries on his vital parts of the body.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The driver of the offending vehicle namely Rahul Khan (respondent no.8) came near Ashok Kumar and his cousin and number of his vehicle was got noted down by cousin of the deceased.

Meanwhile, a three wheeler of their village came from Palwal with passengers and when passengers started shifting Ashok Kumar to Palwal for his treatment, the driver of offending vehicle fled from the spot.
On reaching General Hospital at Palwal, Ashok Kumar was declared 'brought dead' by the doctors at the hospital.
Post mortem of deceased was conducted and on the statement of cousin brother of the deceased, FIR No.22 dated 22.01.2020, under Sections 379, 304-A IPC was lodged at Police Station Chandhut.

4. Claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short - the Act) was filed by widow (respondent no.1), minor daughters and son (respondents no.2 to 4), parents (respondents no.5 and 6) and brother (respondent no.7) of the deceased.
Respondents no.8 and 9 are 2024:PHHC:023440 driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
5. The learned Tribunal, on the basis of evidence recorded in the case, partly allowed the claim petition with costs.

The claimants were held entitled to compensation of Rs. 22,55,900/-, out of which 40% amount was ordered to be paid to the widow, 15% each to the three children and 15% to the mother of the deceased, along with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing the claim petition till its realization.
The appellant Insurance Company was held liable to pay the compensation.

6. The learned Tribunal assessed the aforesaid compensation in the following manner :-

Learned counsel for the appellant Insurance Company, at the outset, has argued that in the joint written statement filed by driver and owner of the offending vehicle, they have completely denied that any accident has been caused by their vehicle and it is a case of false implication 2024:PHHC:023440 of the vehicle in question.
The main reason behind this argument is that in the FIR, number of the offending vehicle was written as HR-50-F-3301 but later, in the claim petition, it was mentioned as HR-52-F-3301.

Therefore, the identity of the offending vehicle being in dispute,
the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal are liable to be set aside on this ground alone.
It has been further submitted that in the challan presented under Section 173 Cr.P.C., the number of vehicle mentioned is also different.

So, the main point that the accident was not caused by the insured vehicle HR-52-F-3301, which has been falsely implicated just to grab money from the Insurance Company, was to be considered by the Tribunal, which has not been done and the petition deserves dismissal on this count alone.

8. It has further been argued that the learned Tribunal, besides allowing Rs.70,000/- on account of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, further granted a sum of Rs.40,000/- each in favour of four claimants i.e. minor children and mother of the deceased, which is totally erroneous as according to the legal position laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported as 2017 SCC Online SC 1270, reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.
15,000/-, Rs. 40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/- respectively i.e. not more than Rs.70,000/-.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So, it has been prayed that in view of the aforesaid shortcomings, the present appeal filed by the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted.

9. Heard.
10.
The date of accident and lodging of FIR is not in dispute.
The 2024:PHHC:023440 post-mortem report and challan under Section 173 Cr.P.C. has also been proved by documentary evidence brought on record.

The main grievance of the appellant regarding wrong mentioning of registration number of offending vehicle has also been addressed by the learned Tribunal by observing that on perusal of challan, it transpired that initially in the complaint, registration number of offending vehicle was correctly mentioned.
However, later while lodging the FIR, the police official inadvertently committed typographical error but even in the final report, correct number of offending vehicle has been mentioned again.
It was just a clerical mistake on the part of police official, who lodged the FIR.
The learned Tribunal also considered that the manner in which the accident took place and prompt lodging of FIR thereafter shows that there was hardly any time for manipulation.
It was further added that even driver of the offending vehicle did not dare to step in the witness-box, which draws adverse inference against him.

sentences.text: The proceedings before the learned Tribunal are civil in nature and facts have been proved on the basis of preponderance of probability.
Even if there was some mistake in the paper work regarding one or two digits or numbers, that has hardly any effect on merits of the case.

12. The learned Tribunal, relying on the case Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram and others reported as 2018(3) Law Herald (SC) 2410, also granted consortium to claimants being spouse, children and mother.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The loss of consortium was again considered by the higher Bench of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 (arising out of SLP (Civil) No.28548 of 2014) 2024:PHHC:023440 titled as United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and Ors.

entities.text:
United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract of the said judgment is as under :-
"b) Loss of Consortium Loss of Consortium, in legal parlance, was historically given a narrow meaning to be awarded only to the spouse i.e. the right of the spouse to the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, society, solace, affection and sexual relations with his or her mate.
The loss of companionship, love, care and protection, etc., the spouse is entitled to get, has to be compensated appropriately.

The concept of non-pecuniary damage for loss of consortium is one of the major heads for awarding compensation in various jurisdictions such as the United States of America,
Australia, etc.
English courts have recognised the right of a spouse to get compensation even during the period of temporary disablement.

In Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Nanu Ram & Ors., this Court interpreted "consortium" to be a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.

entities.text:
Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v.
Nanu Ram & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse.
Parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.
Filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love and affection, and their role in the family unit.
Modern jurisdictions world-over have recognized that the value of a child's consortium far exceeds the economic value of the compensation awarded in the case of the death of a child.
Most jurisdictions permit parents to be awarded compensation under loss of consortium on the death of a child.
The amount awarded to the parents is the compensation for loss of love and affection, care and companionship of the deceased child.

National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Suman And Others on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/130850349/
4

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd vs Suman And Others on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims, or their families, in cases of genuine claims.
In case where a parent has lost their minor child, or unmarried son or daughter, the parents are entitled to be awarded loss of consortium under the head of Filial Consortium.
Parental Consortium is awarded to the children who lose the care and protection of their parents in motor vehicle accidents.
The amount to be awarded for loss consortium will be as per the amount fixed in Pranay Sethi (supra).
At this stage, we consider it necessary to 2024:PHHC:023440 provide uniformity with respect to the grant of consortium, and loss of love and affection.
Several Tribunals and High Courts have been awarding compensation for both loss of consortium and loss of love and affection.
The Constitution Bench in Pranay Sethi (supra), has recognized only three conventional heads under which compensation can be awarded viz. loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses.
In Magma General (supra), this Court gave a comprehensive interpretation to consortium to include spousal consortium, parental consortium, as well as filial consortium.
Loss of love and affection is comprehended in loss of consortium.
The Tribunals and High Courts are directed to award compensation for loss of consortium, which is a legitimate conventional head.

There is no justification to award compensation towards loss of love and affection as a separate head."
13.

The learned Tribunal has granted consortium to the widow, children and mother i.e.
Rs.40,000/- each, in view of the case Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur (supra).
The same has been lightly granted.
14. The learned Tribunal has correctly held that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

Further, perusal of the relevant documents i.e. driving license of the driver, registration certificate and insurance cover note of the offending vehicle reveals that there is no violation of any sort by driver and owner of the offending vehicle.
So, the appellant Insurance Company is certainly liable to pay the compensation, as directed.
There is no ground to interfere in the lawful order passed by the learned Tribunal.
The appeal is without any merit and is therefore, dismissed in limine.
16. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of along with this judgment.

February 15, 2024 (GURBIR SINGH)
